title: repo-analyst joined evaluation trial
description: One trial as the aggregate consumes it. This is NOT a manifest result contract: a trial run cannot validate against it, because a workflow program cannot see its own effective bundle hash, provider snapshot, or verified override identity. Those exist only in the run-started metadata the run itself emits. The trial writes what it can observe, a trusted host step joins the run identity from that run's trace, and the joined record is what repo-analyst-aggregate.json validates. Splitting it this way keeps the identities attributable to the run that produced them rather than to a value the workflow could have invented.

passed.description: Whether the frozen expectation held. A trial that cannot decide is a failure, never a pass.

detail.description: Why the expectation held or did not. Bounded and payload-free.

run_identity.description: Filled by the trusted host step from this run's own run-started metadata. A schema-only hash would not prove the evaluated component or provider was the same, so these are the identities that make a trial attributable.

override_source_hash.description: Present only on a candidate trial. Absent on a baseline, which is how the aggregate tells the two apart without trusting the declared subject.
